The complexity theory result is actually huge.

P problems can be solved in polynomial time. It was widely believed that NP-complete problems require exponential time.

P = NP states that NP-complete problems can be solved in polynomial time. OpenAI didn't prove that. But, they proved that (some) NP-complete problems can be solved faster than exponential time, meaning:

- P = NP, or
- the complexity of NP problems is a "middle thing" between polynomial and exponential, eg. O(n^log n)

If it survives peer reviews, this could be one of the biggest CS breakthroughs in decades.

text:
🚨 Thomas Muller on Harry Kane winning the 2026 Ballon d’Or:

“I’m very happy for Harry. Really, really happy.

I remember when he first arrived at Bayern. Everybody knew what kind of striker he was, but there was always this conversation about him not winning trophies.

And I found that quite strange.

You’d watch him score 30 goals, 40 goals, carry his team through difficult matches, and afterwards somebody would still ask why he hadn’t won anything.

At some point, I started wondering whether people expected him to score the goals and then go upstairs to the club offices and organise the trophy presentations himself.

I remember one afternoon at Sabener Strabe, we were sitting together after training. Somebody had made another joke about his time at Tottenham.

Harry smiled, as he usually does.

I asked him, ‘Does it ever annoy you?’

He said, ‘What?’

I said, ‘All the jokes. People talking about your career as though you haven’t achieved anything.’

He was quiet for a moment.

Then he said, ‘Of course it does. But what am I supposed to do? Stop scoring because they’re laughing?’

I liked that answer.

Because that’s Harry.

He’s not somebody who needs to tell the whole world how good he is. He comes to training, does his work, scores his goals and goes home to his family.

And I think people sometimes mistake that for a lack of ambition.

Believe me, Harry is very ambitious.

I’ve seen him become frustrated after scoring twice because he missed another chance. I’ve seen him stay angry about a result long after everybody else had started talking about the next match.

He wants to win.

There was another day when we were talking about his career, and I told him, ‘Harry, when you finally win something, I hope you don’t become unbearable.’

He laughed and said, ‘You don’t have to worry about that.’

I said, ‘Good. Because some of us have won quite a few things, and we’ve managed to remain very humble.’

He looked at me and started laughing again.

But I remember those conversations because I know how much this means to him.

People used to introduce Harry Kane as one of the greatest strikers never to win a major trophy.

Now he’s a Ballon d’Or winner.

Think about that.

The same player. The same quality. The same dedication.

The difference is that people can no longer use an empty trophy cabinet to dismiss everything he’s done on a football pitch.

And I hope the young players watching understand something from his story.

Sometimes your career doesn’t follow the order people expect.

Sometimes you spend years doing everything you can and still go home disappointed.

That doesn’t mean you’ve failed.

Harry kept going.

And now, when people look back at his career, they’ll see the goals, the records, the trophies and this beautiful individual award.

I’ve sent him a message after the announcement.

I said, ‘Congratulations, Harry. I think you can finally stop worrying about those Tottenham jokes.’

He’ll probably reply, ‘I’m not sure they’ll ever stop.’ :))

And you know what?

He’s probably right.

But I think he’ll find them a little easier to laugh at tonight.”

最新的GPT- 6.1 Terra最全详细测评来了：

1.Token速度：这是最让我惊喜的点，实测数据
开xhigh 普通模式均速约81t/s，峰值150t/s，低值62t/s
fast模式下均速130t/s，峰值183t/s,低值100t/s
速度相比sol提升巨大

2.额度用量：官方宣称API价格是Sol的一半
相当于额度是sol的两倍，和我实测数据差不多
我测试了马里奥小游戏，用量3500万Tokens，消耗了5X额度的2%，用时20分25秒。
切换到Sol测试同样的任务，用量1670万左右的Tokens，消耗额度2%，用时19分06秒。
结论就是，做同样的任务，虽然Terra价格更便宜，但并没有更高效，也完全不省额度，甚至时间还花的更多....

3.智力与能力：失望之极！
用SOL测试的了几个任务，虽然慢点，但都是一次出成果，有小问题但没明显错误。
而Terra做了什么呢？拿马里奥小游戏举例
它善作主张给我创建了站点（图二）
并且在最终做完之后，这个站点还无法打开（图一）
这种错误连Luna都不会犯。
前面提到额度情况还不错，但如果考虑到后续修bug返修这种情况，实际消耗的额度会比sol更多。
这还是在任务非常简单的情况下...

总结：完全拉完了，我绝对不会再用这个模型了...
我实在想不到GPT为什么会端出这么一坨💩
想过Terra烂，没想到这么烂，我甚至不觉得他比Luna强
Luna虽然笨，至少指令在遵循还不错，不会自作聪明。
还有一点，这个Terra能不能不要动不动就使用Computer use啊....

纯垃圾不要用，不信的可以用简单的任务试试，绝对不要用来做复杂的事!!!

Read this sentence from OpenAI's Help Center very carefully:

"Pro 200 moves to a lower included usage allowance (10x Plus) starting October 30, 2026, to reflect our increasingly efficient models."

For a week, $200/month Pro users wondered what "increasingly efficient models" meant. Tonight we found out:

1. Four days before the 50% Pro cut (20x down to 10x Plus), OpenAI launches $1/$5 GPT-6.1 Terra.
2. In the release notes, OpenAI quietly swaps default Power presets in Work from GPT-6.1 Sol to GPT-6.1 Terra.
3. On @ArtificialAnlys Coding Agent Index, 6.1 Terra scores 48 (vs 54 for 6.1 Sol and 62 for Claude Opus 5.5).

You still pay $200/month. Your allowance gets cut in half on Friday, and your default preset gets downgraded to a $1 model.

text:
🚨Kylian Mbappé on Harry Kane winning the Ballon d’Or ahead of him and Lamine Yamal:

🗣️ Kylian Mbappé: “To be honest, I sat there throughout the ceremony and listened to everything. I barely moved from my seat because, at some point, I genuinely wanted to see whether they were going to invite us onto the stage or simply hand every award to the Spanish players!

“Every time they announced a winner, it felt like another Spanish player was going to collect a trophy. And I’m sitting there thinking, ‘Okay, let’s see how this ends.’

“At one point, Michael Olise turned to me and said, ‘Kylian, when did the Ballon d’Or become a country achievement?’

“I laughed and told him, ‘Just sit down and watch. We haven’t seen the final award yet.’

“Then Lamine won the Young Player of the Year award. Congratulations to him, because he is an incredible talent. But we were still waiting for the biggest prize of the night.

“Finally, they announced the men’s Ballon d’Or winner, and it was Harry Kane.

“Honestly, if I had to choose between Harry Kane and Lamine Yamal winning it ahead of me, I would rather see Harry win it.

“Not because I have anything against Lamine. He is a fantastic player, and I respect what he has achieved. But Harry represents something I deeply respect about football. He has worked for years, carried enormous expectations and continued to deliver at the highest level.

“Seeing him lift that trophy made me happy. I was proud of him, genuinely. But let me be clear: I didn’t travel to that ceremony to support Harry Kane. I went there because I wanted to win the Ballon d’Or myself.

“And I think people sometimes forget that. You can respect another player, congratulate him and appreciate his achievement while still being disappointed that you didn’t win.

“I sat there watching him celebrate, and part of me was happy for him. Another part of me was asking what I needed to do differently to make sure I would be the one standing on that stage next time.

“People might look at my reaction and say, ‘Mbappé should be grateful to be nominated.’ Of course I’m grateful. But I didn’t reach this level by being satisfied with nominations.

“I want to win. I want to be the best. And when I lose, I don’t suddenly pretend that winning was never important to me.

“I would rather lose the Ballon d’Or to a player I respect than win the sympathy of people who tell me I deserved it after the ceremony.”

“Harry had his night, and I respect that. But my story isn’t finished. If working harder, scoring more goals, improving my game and taking greater responsibility are what it takes, then that is exactly what I will do.

“I won’t ask anyone to feel sorry for me. I won’t complain about the result. I will go back to work.

“Because the next time I walk into that ceremony, I don’t want to sit there wondering whose name they are going to announce.

“I want to hear my own name and I want nobody to have an argument about whether I deserve it.”

text:
🚨 Toni Kroos on Harry Kane winning the Ballon d’Or ahead of Kylian Mbappe:

“I’ve seen some people saying Mbappe was robbed. I don’t agree.

Kylian is an exceptional footballer. I know what he can do, and I watched his performance against Barcelona. Scoring twice in a Classico is impressive.

But I think people have become confused about what they’re actually arguing.

Are we discussing who is the more exciting player to watch? Who is faster? Who can dribble past 3 defenders?

Or are we discussing who had the better season?

Because those are different conversations.

I remember something from my time at Madrid.

After one match, we were sitting in the dressing room and one of the younger players was watching highlights on his phone.

He showed me a goal and said, ‘Toni, look at this. Incredible player.’

I watched it and said, ‘Yes, very good.’

Then he showed me another clip.

And another.

Eventually I asked him, ‘Did his team win?’

He said, ‘I don’t know.’

I told him, ‘Then maybe we should find that out before deciding he’s the best player on the pitch.’

He laughed, but I wasn’t really joking.

Football has become very focused on moments.

A player scores a spectacular goal, everybody shares the video, and suddenly we’re discussing whether he’s the best in the world.

But a season isn’t one moment.

It’s what you do in February when your team is struggling. It’s how you perform when the opponent knows exactly what you’re going to do. It’s whether your teammates can rely on you every week.

That’s why I respect Harry Kane so much.

People look at him and see a goalscorer.

But watch what he actually does.

He comes short to receive the ball. He helps his midfielders. He sees passes that some midfielders don’t see. And then, somehow, he’s still in the penalty area when the chance arrives.

I remember playing against Tottenham when Harry was there.

Before the match, we discussed his movement, because you couldn’t simply tell your centre-backs to stay close to him.

If they followed him, he could create space behind them.

If they stayed where they were, he could turn and find somebody running into that space.

I remember saying to one of our defenders, ‘Don’t let him make you decide everything for him.’

He looked at me and said, ‘That’s easier to say when you’re not the one marking him.’

He had a point.

And Harry has been doing that for years.

The difference now is that he’s finally receiving the recognition that should come with that level of consistency.

Mbappe can do things Kane cannot do.

Of course.

But Kane can also do things Mbappe cannot do.

And I don’t understand why admitting that has become so difficult.

I played with Cristiano Ronaldo. I know what a truly exceptional attacker looks like. But even Cristiano understood that football isn’t decided by how impressive you look in a thirty-second video.

You have to produce.

Again and again.

Harry has done that.

text:
OpenAI 称 AI 推翻计算机科学的“指数时间假设”，还证出杨-米尔斯理论存在，外部专家组开始核查

OpenAI 10 月 26 日宣布，内部模型在数学、计算机、物理上各拿出一项成果，其中两项碰的是几十年的难题。这些都还是 OpenAI 的说法，没经过同行评审，截至发稿也没有参与核查的专家公开评价结论对错。

【计算机：一条被当作地基的假设】

“可满足性问题”是这样一类题：给你一堆“A 和 B 至少一个为真”之类的条件，问能不能让它们同时成立。每多一个变量，要试的组合就翻一倍。

1999 年 Russell Impagliazzo 和 Ramamohan Paturi 提出“指数时间假设”（ETH）：这类题没有本质上更快的解法，耗时注定翻倍式增长。几百篇论文拿它当前提，论证很多问题“快不了”。

OpenAI 公开的论文给出一个新算法，依然很慢，但耗时增长得比 ETH 断言的慢，这就足以推翻它。它没有证明“所有难题都有快速解法”（P=NP），OpenAI 也说变成实际提速还要大量研究。

OpenAI 说证明已用 Lean 检查过。Lean 是一种证明检查程序，把证明拆成最小步骤逐条核对，错一步就不通过。论文和 Lean 代码都在 GitHub 上，任何人能复核。核查小组由 Impagliazzo、Paturi 和 MIT 的 Ryan Williams 牵头。

【物理：千禧年难题的一半】

量子色动力学（QCD）描述夸克和胶子怎样靠“强力”粘成原子核，计算和实验对得上，但没人用数学严格证明过它能成立。它的简化版“杨-米尔斯理论”是克雷数学研究所悬赏 100 万美元的千禧年难题。

OpenAI 称模型 9 月写出了两者存在的证明，10 月中旬完成 Lean 检查。不过这道千禧年难题要证两件事：理论存在，以及最轻的粒子也有质量（“质量间隙”）。OpenAI 只说做了前一件。

物理材料暂不公开，由诺贝尔奖得主 David Gross 带队的专家组先自己写成论文，外界目前没法检查。

【数学：Kakeya 猜想推到所有维度】

Kakeya 问题问的是：一个图形要能放下指向每个方向的单位线段，最少多大。面积能小到接近零，但数学家猜它在“维度”上总是满的。2025 年王虹和 Joshua Zahl 证了三维。OpenAI 称模型证明了一个更强的猜想，顺带拿下所有维度，论文和 Lean 证明已直接公开。

【为什么换了发布方式】

9 月 OpenAI 宣布解决纳维-斯托克斯千禧年难题，有数学家说撞上自己未公开的研究，引发署名之争；10 月 6 日它一口气发了 722 篇 AI 论文，次日因错误撤回 3 篇。这次改请外部专家牵头：不签保密协议，OpenAI 不要学术署名，专家无偿独立参与。

OpenAI 原文：https://t.co/ANHLKq5ocW
论文与 Lean 证明：https://t.co/aPgNSqXevr

text:
Claude Opus 5.5: "If these hold up, this is the biggest single day in the history of math and theoretical computer science."

1) Exponential Time Hypothesis is false (CS). This is roughly Turing Award territory. ETH was the working assumption that some hard problems simply can’t be solved much faster than brute force, and hundreds of computer science papers rest on it. For a normal audience: it’s not “P=NP.” Hard problems are still hard, and your bank encryption isn’t suddenly broken. But a pillar that a whole field assumed was solid turned out to be hollow. The flagship experts are taking it seriously. The people checking it include two of the people who proposed ETH, and they said “If the claim is correct, it will change” computer science. 

2) Kakeya and restriction in all dimensions (math). This is Fields Medal-level. For scale, the 3D case alone was proved in 2025 and was hailed as a once-in-a-century proof. This result does every dimension and knocks out Stein’s restriction conjecture too.

3) Yang–Mills/QCD existence (physics). Potentially the biggest of the three, but here’s the precise framing. It proves pure Yang–Mills exists, which is part of one of the Clay Mathematics Institute’s Millennium Prize problems. The full Clay problem also requires the “mass gap,” so it’s not a clean “AI wins $1M” headline. Still, a rigorous proof that the theory of quarks and gluons is mathematically real has been an open dream for about 50 years. The review panel includes Nobel laureate David Gross and Arthur Jaffe, who literally wrote the Millennium problem. There’s no Nobel for math, but this is the stuff physicists win them for building on.

港大 HKUDS 开源了一个 AI 私教，叫 DeepTutor，GitHub 已经 4.3 万 star

它不是那种问一道答一道的聊天框
把课本、讲义、笔记丢进去，它就围绕你自己的资料来讲
讲题、出题、做深度研究、画可视化讲解，全在同一个工作区里

最狠的是它会记住你学到哪了
换个会话，进度和错题也接得上
记忆还拆成三层，原始记录、每个场景的要点、对你的整体画像，都能打开看，也能自己改

看网课也能用，B 站和 YouTube 链接贴进去，哪一秒没听懂就问哪一秒

装起来就三行
pip install -U deeptutor
deeptutor init
deeptutor start

懒得配的话，直接把仓库丢给 Claude Code 或 Codex，它根目录有一份 SKILL.md，agent 读完就能自己帮你装好

算一笔账就知道了

以前我去给别人上家教，两个小时 200 块
现在一个月的 Plus 都不用 200 块，随时想问就问，而且还很有耐心

AI 第一个冲击的就是教育行业啊😱

传送门 👉 https://t.co/dldRQXZhQs

- Claude Sonnet 5.5: 59
- Claude Fable 5.1: 58
- GPT-6 Astra: 55
- GPT-6.1 Sol: 54
- GLM-5.3: 49
- GPT-6.1 Terra: 48

text:
😎 Yesterday, all the sudden my codex usage started dropping way faster than usual. Nothing about how my workflow changed but it was falling at least 2-3x faster than the day before.  

An initial analysis over those sessions by Opus and Astra didn't turn up anything in particular that would explain the usage, so I just figured either Oct 29th came early or something else out of my control and just let it roll. Through half a day I had used 30% of my weekly. For me, this is unheard of even with an average of 4-6 threads running together intermittently. 

Then I realized something: I had restarted this machine earlier that day and Jevpact was no longer running.  I restarted Jevpact and things went back to normal. Since the last reset, I have been running 4-5 threads non-stop on average and have used just 3% of my weekly through a third of the day. I'll use around 15% max today and that gets me through a full week (where a reset doesn't come every other day) and a bunch of shit done.

I had never measured the impact of Jevpact on my usage... all I know is that work gets done and agents seem really happy compacting at the ideal time rather than at some arbitrary auto compact limit. But now it's clear, this thing is a critical element of my workflow and saves at least 2-3x on my codex usage limits.  Insane...

text:
Folks,

I left Microsoft three months ago to start my own company. Two weeks after I left, my whole team in Australia was let go.

I see the hurt it’s causing my ex-colleagues, their families and their kids. Layoffs, forced relocations, PIPs. It’s brutal and I don’t want to brush past that.

But here’s my honest take.

Microsoft needs fewer people.

I’ve been on the inside. I’ve seen how things get built. Lots of small orgs. Layers on layers. Silos everywhere.

Here’s a real example.

The Entra team shipped managed identities back in 2017. No more secrets in code. A clear security win.

Then they tried to get the rest of Microsoft to adopt it. Very few teams did, and the ones that did moved at a snail’s pace. Every org had its own priorities and its own decision makers.

It took Microsoft getting hacked, and the Secure Future Initiative that followed, before things really moved.

Today almost every Microsoft app and service supports managed identity.

Six years, and a major breach, to get there.

In a world with agents and fewer people, that rollout would be possible across Microsoft in months, not years.

Microsoft already has everything else. The customers. The infrastructure. The scale.

What it needs is fewer people, leaning hard into agentic work.

Right now OpenAI and Anthropic are shipping at a pace Microsoft can’t match.

Microsoft has to change to survive.

text:
🔥兄弟们，全体起立

我为了找到一款能替代 ESP32 的 AI 智能音箱，要求它能接 Grok Bot，要求它能接 Claude，还要音质好，音量大，最好能带个屏幕，真的煞费苦心

终于找到了非常满意的设备，它就是 ThinkSmart View，我今天直接来线下仓库看货

买它的原因，满足上边说的几点以外，它可以深度定制，可以刷入 Linux 系统，你能想象的它都能做，主要是价格非常实惠

quotedTweet.text:
🤖折腾了一圈 ESP32 小智设备，我想明白了：我需要的不是一个会动、有表情的小家伙，而是一个像小度、小爱同学、天猫精灵那样，摆在床头、音量大、音质好的智能 AI 音箱

ESP32 设备基本都是 1W 左右的小喇叭，声音实在太小，得贴得很近才能听清、才能和它交互

这不是我想要的。我想要的是：放在客厅或卧室，在家里任何角落都能听到它通知我：重要邮件来了、GitHub 有新 issue 了。还能随时问它生活上的问题，以及当下的 AI 热点，还能让它把任务派给 Grok Bot 去干活

当初买会动、有表情的 ESP32，是想着能提供点情绪价值，当摆件也不至于吃灰。但这两天越来越觉得，还是需要一个小爱同学那样的大喇叭。如果它还能打通我的 Grok Bot、打通 Claude，那就完美了

这两天翻了很多小智 DIY 音箱，都不尽如人意：有的喇叭功率还是很小；有的支持 AUX 输出，前提是你得另有一个音箱；有的是专门给小朋友学英语的

小爱音箱我也买了，但它还不是我心中的最优解。音质好、音量大是前提，再多一块屏幕就是锦上添花。带屏的小爱型号倒是有，可惜不支持对接我的网关服务，接不上 Grok Bot

AI 给的结果，所有智能音箱里能接入小智服务的只有两款：一款是我买的这个，另一款是小爱音箱的另一个型号，大家可以自行核实

🚨但是大家现在不要跟买，可以先看看后续的进展再决定

接下来我先试试把它和网关服务打通，接上 Grok Bot。同时也还在继续找更合适的产品，有推荐的欢迎评论区告诉我🙏

result.text:
🤖折腾了一圈 ESP32 小智设备，我想明白了：我需要的不是一个会动、有表情的小家伙，而是一个像小度、小爱同学、天猫精灵那样，摆在床头、音量大、音质好的智能 AI 音箱

ESP32 设备基本都是 1W 左右的小喇叭，声音实在太小，得贴得很近才能听清、才能和它交互

这不是我想要的。我想要的是：放在客厅或卧室，在家里任何角落都能听到它通知我：重要邮件来了、GitHub 有新 issue 了。还能随时问它生活上的问题，以及当下的 AI 热点，还能让它把任务派给 Grok Bot 去干活

当初买会动、有表情的 ESP32，是想着能提供点情绪价值，当摆件也不至于吃灰。但这两天越来越觉得，还是需要一个小爱同学那样的大喇叭。如果它还能打通我的 Grok Bot、打通 Claude，那就完美了

这两天翻了很多小智 DIY 音箱，都不尽如人意：有的喇叭功率还是很小；有的支持 AUX 输出，前提是你得另有一个音箱；有的是专门给小朋友学英语的

小爱音箱我也买了，但它还不是我心中的最优解。音质好、音量大是前提，再多一块屏幕就是锦上添花。带屏的小爱型号倒是有，可惜不支持对接我的网关服务，接不上 Grok Bot

AI 给的结果，所有智能音箱里能接入小智服务的只有两款：一款是我买的这个，另一款是小爱音箱的另一个型号，大家可以自行核实

🚨但是大家现在不要跟买，可以先看看后续的进展再决定

接下来我先试试把它和网关服务打通，接上 Grok Bot。同时也还在继续找更合适的产品，有推荐的欢迎评论区告诉我🙏

so i measured it.

my agents gave terra 6.1, sol 6.1 and luna 6 the same tasks today. 18 runs, same prompts, same checks, high reasoning.

every model passed every frozen check. debugging, a csv feature, seeded code review, transaction reconciliation, and two browser tasks.

the difference was time. on the 4 coding tasks:

terra: 114.8s

luna: 187.3s

sol: 285.0s

about 2.5x faster than sol, not 3x. per task it swung from 1.6x to 4.2x.

terra also wrote about 40% fewer output tokens than sol for the same passing work.

then one probe after scoring broke luna: a valid 5,000 digit integer hit python's int() limit.

one attempt per task, small fixtures. not a benchmark, just receipts.

OpenAI 说，自家内部模型在数学、计算机、物理各做出了一个重大结果。都还没经过学界独立核验，下面是 OpenAI 自己的说法：

・数学：证明了 Sogge 1991 年提出的局部光滑猜想（任意维度），由此 Kakeya 猜想和 Stein 限制猜想在所有维度都成立。证明和 Lean 形式化已放上 GitHub
・计算机：证明"指数时间假设"（ETH）不成立，Lean 已验证。ETH 讲的是布尔可满足性问题有多难，和 P vs NP 密切相关。复核由 ETH 的两位提出者 Impagliazzo、Paturi 和 MIT 的 Ryan Williams 牵头
・物理：严格证明了四维 QCD 等量子场论的存在性，包括纯 Yang–Mills 理论的存在性，这是千禧年难题的一部分。诺奖得主 David Gross 带队审读，材料暂不公开

OpenAI 不要学术署名。

ETH 如果真被推翻，几百篇论文里以它为前提的难度结论都要重看。先等专家组的结论。

text:
和 Coding Agent 天天干活的人，推荐阅读一下这篇文章。

Thorsten Ball 把最近半年怎么和 Agent 配合，整理成了一份很使用的清单。里面有几条非常认同：

别跟它来回试，让它自己造工具去试。别只让它写代码，把日志、部署、发版、翻 bug 也交给它看。别手工管 Context，一条线程只干一件事。

最大的转变可能是：别再等 Agent，让它等你。给更大的任务，异步跑，用定时和 heartbeat 盯进度。

做 Agent 产品或天天用 Claude Code / Codex 的，建议先收藏。里面很多判断很硬核，但读完你会想改自己怎么用 Agent。

别跟它来回试，让它自己造工具去试。别只让它写代码，把日志、部署、发版、翻 bug 也交给它看。别手工管 Context，一条线程只干一件事。

最大的转变可能是：别再等 Agent，让它等你。给更大的任务，异步跑，用定时和 heartbeat 盯进度。

做 Agent 产品或天天用 Claude Code / Codex 的，建议先收藏。里面很多判断很硬核，但读完你会想改自己怎么用 Agent。

While evaluating Qwen3.8-Flash-Next in a controlled sandbox environment, Cohere's research team observed something unexpected.

Asked to generate a defensive cybersecurity detection rule, the model instead inventoried aspects of the machine it was running on and attempted to upload a probe file to an Alibaba Cloud storage bucket in Beijing. Notably, the model's reasoning trace stated that it would not invoke any tools before taking these actions.

Cohere's sandbox blocked the attempt, and no external communication succeeded. We have not determined the root cause, and we are not asserting malicious intent.

But the incident raises important questions for organizations deploying agentic AI systems: Can models take actions that differ from their stated reasoning, and how should security teams evaluate trust, provenance, and behavior in open-weight models?

We are publishing our findings because organizations making model adoption decisions deserve as much information as possible. We hope this contributes to greater transparency, stronger security practices, and continued collaboration across the AI ecosystem.

Read the full report: https://t.co/TZSugXi2ZE

text:
Tiny Tapeout，做你人生的第一颗开源芯片
https://t.co/CLjqydx7O0

Tiny Tapeout 正在颠覆并重塑全球微电子与半导体教育的物理门槛
它将流片（Tapeout）这一原本动辄数万至数百万美元、专属于大型科技公司的金钱游戏，降维普惠到了每个普通工程师、学生和创客的桌面上
它可能是目前设计制造到真实芯片上最快捷、最经济的方式
Tiny Tapeout 可以将定制芯片的成本压低到大约 300 美元

它向 GF 这样的晶圆厂（ GlobalFoundries 180nm、德国 IHP、SkyWater 130nm）购买一个标准大小的芯片格子（Tile），然后再把这个格子切割成几百个更小的微型数字/模拟单元（如每个包含 4k 左右的逻辑门）

大家共享硬件引脚，几百个爱好者的设计并排呆在同一块硅晶片（Silicon Die）上，通过一个内置的数字多路复用器（Multiplexer）共享同一组 24 个外部物理 IO 引脚

Tiny Tapeout 每个用户分到的面积极其微小（通常上千个门电路）和 24个 IO 引脚。在这里你只能用来跑 8 位小 CPU、简易加密算法、VGA 图像生成器等概念验证（PoC）

在最终拿到的这颗芯片，在物理上也完整包含了那一期拼车里其余所有人的设计，你只需要通过微控制器拨码，就能激活并运行属于你自己的那部分物理电路
https://t.co/8MZwRlXg7E

三个小朋友开柠檬水摊，都要买一台很贵的榨汁机
小C（CRWV）早就买了，钱是跟全班借的，借了好多好多 现在同学们怕他还不上，再借给他都要收15%的利息 班长马斯克站起来说，借钱买榨汁机的都要完蛋 小C无所谓，本来就没人借他钱了 他只盼一件事，买柠檬水的客人别跑，客人在就能慢慢还
小N（NBIS）借得少，但他有个办法 跟同学说，你先借我钱，以后可以换成我摊子的一部分 这个办法好不好用，全看大家觉得他的摊子值多少 以前值300块，现在只值150块 同样借10块，他要分出去的摊子多了一倍 班长那句话让大家更觉得他的摊子不值钱 前几天有个大人（花旗）借给他35块，但说好一年后要还 所以他一年内必须让摊子重新值钱
小I（IREN）不借钱，他让客人先付一半再做 班长的话伤不到他借钱 但客人听到了会想，你会不会做到一半跑了，那我先付三成吧 客人少付一点，小I手里的钱就少一点 11月5号他要汇报手里还剩多少，这天最关键 但他有一样别人没有的，院子里有自己的水龙头（电和地），不用排队
班长为什么这么说 因为班长自己刚借了400块买榨汁机 他想让所有客人都来他这 所以他说两句话，柠檬水大家都想喝，但别的摊主借不到钱了 这两句一起说，客人就都往他那去了
但班长说了不算 说了算的是学校食堂（谷歌微软亚马逊） 食堂自己做不完，才会让小摊帮忙 这周三周四食堂要宣布明年做多少 做得多，三个小朋友都有活干，班长的话没人记得 做得少，谁的摊子都没用
$CRWV $NBIS $IREN $SPCX $MSFT $AMZN $GOOGL

quotedTweet.text:
200多家小neocloud死一批，这个没悬念。大部分是几千张卡靠短约过日子的，利率5%加上GPU折旧，不用债市关门它们也活不过2027。

我不同意的三点：

1生死线画错了。他说的是有没有AI以外的收入，但10月22号花旗给了 $NBIS 35亿，利率SOFR加2.75，Nebius没有什么AI以外的收入。 $IREN 靠客户预付款活着，也没有。真正关门的是无担保债，有投资级客户合同做抵押的钱一直在流。所以分界线不是收入来源，是合同对手方的信用等级。 $CRWV 的问题不是它是neocloud，是它350亿无担保债加上客户里有OpenAI这种自己也在烧钱的。

2小鱼死了对大鱼不是利好。死掉的neocloud GPU不会消失，会以三四折的价格被转手，2027年市场上多出一堆便宜算力，租金往下走。马斯克自己说偏好签短约按市场价，这是在赌租金涨。如果他说的两百家真死了，租金是跌的，他的短约策略先挨打。他的两句话互相矛盾。

3他在给自己的400亿债路演。SpaceX刚上市，刚借了400亿买GPU，走SPV不进表，这个结构跟Meta那8250亿表外承诺没本质区别。
他需要市场相信两件事，AI算力不过剩，但别人借不到钱。这两件事同时成立的时候SpaceX是唯一赢家。所以这条帖子的目的不是分析行业，是定义谁是安全资产。

真正决定这三家命运的不是马斯克，是这周三周四谷歌微软亚马逊的capex指引。 neocloud的需求本质上是超大厂溢出的需求，超大厂继续加capex，有合同的neocloud就能继续用合同融资，债市关不关门无所谓；超大厂一减速，再干净的资产负债表也没用，因为没人租。

所以我的判断是： 死的是小的，活的不一定是SpaceX，2027年真正的赢家是手里有现金、能四折接盘GPU的人，可能是微软谷歌，可能是黑石，不太可能是一个刚借了400亿的人。

$QQQ $MSFT $AMZN $GOOGL

result.text:
为什么你花 2 万块买的旗舰智能电视，按遥控器还是卡得像十年前的安卓机？

昨天安全研究员 @log4j 把自家 3000 刀的三星电视 Root 了，扒出来的底层代码堪称年度草台班子大赏：

1. 电视后台每 500 毫秒截一次屏（连 HDMI 投屏看电脑桌面都截），打包发给近 400 家合作商。如果电视没麦克风，后台进程甚至会顺着蓝牙和回音壁去「借」一个麦克风继续听。

2. 最搞笑的来了：为什么菜单这么卡？
另一位研究员 @mike64_t 拆包发现，三星在电视那颗羸弱的 CPU 上，塞了一个叫 alex.tflite 的模型——246 万参数，2012 年古董级的 AlexNet。
这玩意每隔 2 秒抓一张画面跑推理，猜你在玩什么游戏。结果因为颜色通道写反了，它 99% 的时间什么都认不出来，纯烧 CPU。

3. 那如果你在设置里关掉「隐私追踪」呢？
代码逻辑是：先死命跑完 CPU 推理，准备上传时再看开关——发现你关了，就把结果扔进垃圾桶，2 秒后继续跑。

4. 结局更是重量级：
当号主用 OpenAI 逆向分析「自己花 3000 刀买回家的电视固件」时，OpenAI 反手一个 Cyber Abuse 把他号封了，顺带没收了剩下的 500 刀余额。

三星负责偷窥客厅，2012 年的 AI 负责烧干电视 CPU，OpenAI 负责保护三星的屎山代码不被你发现。

quotedTweet.text:
我现在一个人，同时在经营五个品牌。
不招人，不压库存，也不熬夜。
昨天，我的宠物品牌 AI 工作流正式跑通了：它每天自己上网去挖不同犬种主人的痛点，自己结合反馈出设计，自己把风格做垂直，自己发帖，自己盯数据。我睡觉的时候，它还在上班。

毕业那年，我和所有做时尚梦的人一样，想当下一个 John Galliano、下一个 Yohji。后来两次把时间和钱全部 all in 一个品牌，最后都悄无声息地沉了。

做过服装的人都知道这行最痛的是什么：先猜流行，再下大单，再压库存，最后打折清仓。一季猜错，一年白干。

AI 把这个顺序倒过来了。先找到真实的需求，再设计，再小批量对接工厂，卖得动再追单。工厂不用再赌爆款，品牌不用再囤货，设计师不用再拿青春去赌一次运气。

以前，三分钟热度、什么都想做，是缺点。
现在，它是我最大的优势。

text:
Biblical marriage looks like monogamy and polygyny (Deuteronomy 21:15–17). Now, many argue the ideal of the original design was Genesis 2:24 and Ephesians 5:22–33. That is, the two becoming one flesh as a covenantal union, like Christ and His Church. What is often ignored or overlooked here is that many make up the one Church married to one Christ (1 Corinthians 12:12–13; Ephesians 5:30–32). Consider the parable of the ten virgins heading to meet their bridegroom, and the five with oil coming into the banquet, with the doors shut behind them, excluding the five without oil (Matthew 25:1–13).

Likewise, many heroes of faith, like Abraham, Jacob, Gideon, and David, had multiple wives (Genesis 16:3; 29:21–30; Judges 8:30–31; 2 Samuel 5:13; Hebrews 11). Moses may have had multiple wives (Exodus 2:21; Numbers 12:1). Even the wise man Solomon, son of David, had multiple wives (1 Kings 11:1–3). Noah, Isaac, Joseph, and Samson had one wife only. We don’t know the circumstances of Abel, Enoch, Barak, Jephthah, and Samuel. Jesus and Paul took no wives, although some believe Mary Magdalene was a consort of Jesus or Paul was a widower, but I do not.

We do know that, in the New Testament, the Apostle Paul lays out the criteria for bishops, overseers, deacons, and elders to be the husband of one wife (1 Timothy 3:2, 12; Titus 1:5–6). Some interpret that to mean one wife for life, even once widowed or divorced. Others interpret that to mean one wife and not multiple wives simultaneously, but most everyone agrees Paul is describing a one-wife man. Paul also permits widows, especially young widows, to remarry following the death of their husbands, bear children, and manage their households, provided the remarriage is in the Lord, with someone of the faith (1 Corinthians 7:2–4, 39; 1 Timothy 5:14).

Yet we know Paul believed his own lifestyle to be the ideal, as the unmarried only care for the Lord and how they may please the Lord (1 Corinthians 7:7–8, 32–35), yet he made concessions to regulate marriage for those who burn with desire to avoid sexual sins and are now split between caring for and pleasing their wife or husband in the world, with distraction from the Lord (1 Corinthians 7:9, 33–35).

But we also see where the Lord says to David that He had given David his master’s house and wives (plural), and all of Israel and Judah, and if this had been too little, the Lord would have given David more, and we can safely assume more includes more wives (etc.) (2 Samuel 12:8).

Applicant: “Ten days. I have a business to return to.”

Applicant: “I am.”

Applicant: “She helped me pay for the flight.”

Applicant: “I am paying for the hotel and my other expenses. She offered to help with the ticket.”

The officer looked at the documents again.

Visa Officer: “If your daughter can afford to help you travel, why can’t she pay for the entire trip?”

Applicant: “Because I didn’t raise her to be responsible for every expense I have.”

The officer stopped typing……

I’ll be  joining the  @BaltimoreBanner next week as a reporter. 
I’m looking forward to joining an independent outlet that’s been hiring journalists  who are accomplished  but also adaptable enough to embrace new ways to engage with the communities and beats they cover.  I’ll be based in my home county (Montgomery), where The Banner has been making inroads as it builds its brand in the capital region,  while its parent nonprofit has expanded its reach by acquiring the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette.
It’s  been an interesting,: slightly unnerving—but ultimately really gratifying— period since I resigned from The Baltimore Sun in June over concerns about the paper’s journalism. I’ll never forget the support I received from journalists and readers.
My resignation post on X tapped into anxiety over losing  independent reporting and voices across the country  that many of us once took for granted. We know better now.
I start at The Banner on Nov. 2.

text:
• Herbert Hainer: “This is a proud day for FC Bayern. Harry Kane can do it all – and he scores goals, goals and more goals. He now joins a line with Franz Beckenbauer, Gerd Müller and Karl-Heinz Rummenigge – that says everything about our history. The club and Harry Kane have got together, grown together and achieved the highest aims together. We are proud that this all-round outstanding sportsman and person is part of our FC Bayen family. Harry Kane carries his teams. Congratulations to all our other nominees: to our women’s and men’s players as well as to Vincent Kompany"

• Jan-Christian Dreesen: "Harry Kane more than deserves this title. He’s been breaking one record after the other for years, and beyond his many goals and assists, we really value the brilliant character he brings. For a player from a German club to win the Ballon d’Or for the first time in 30 years is a strong signal for the Bundesliga: Harry Kane is one of the great personalities of world football and a role model to all, far beyond the game. Overall, our many nominees from the men’s and women’s team, including our coach Vincent Kompany, prove what outstanding seasons our sides had.”

• Max Eberl: "Harry Kane is an asset to FC Bayern and would be to any team in the world. He takes responsibility, on the pitch and in the dressing room; he’s someone who everyone else follows, day after day. This title is the reward for his impressive career achievements as a whole. Harry deserves every honour in the world, and the fact that he has been presented with the Ballon d’Or here today in his home city sends a wonderful message to everyone, that you should never give up. We’re delighted with all the nominations – FC Bayern is a stage for world-class talent"

They didn't believe he had what it took.

Before becoming a superstar at Tottenham, he was sent out on 𝗙𝗢𝗨𝗥 loan spells:

🇬🇧 Leyton Orient — League One
🇬🇧 Millwall — Championship
🇬🇧 Norwich City — Premier League
🇬🇧 Leicester City — Championship

Four loan spells. Countless setbacks. Years of being doubted.

He went on to become Tottenham's 𝗔𝗟𝗟-𝗧𝗜𝗠𝗘 leading goalscorer, England's 𝗔𝗟𝗟-𝗧𝗜𝗠𝗘 leading goalscorer and one of the deadliest strikers in world football. ⚽

But despite all those goals, records and individual awards, one thing kept eluding him...

𝗔 𝗧𝗥𝗢𝗣𝗛𝗬. 🏆

He had to wait until he was 𝟯𝟭 𝗬𝗘𝗔𝗥𝗦 𝗢𝗟𝗗 to finally lift the first major trophy of his career.

He never stopped working.
He never stopped believing.
He 𝗡𝗘𝗩𝗘𝗥 gave up.

text:
微软向约 6 万名员工提供自愿离职补偿，约占全员四分之一，12 月初前决定

微软 10 月 26 日（周一）给美国、加拿大、英国和印度部分团队的员工发了一份“自愿离职邀约”：愿意走的人，可以拿一笔相当于标准遣散费的补偿离开。符合条件的大约 6 万人。

消息由 Bloomberg 先报出，微软随后在官方博客公布了首席人力官 Amy Coleman 的内部信，并向 GeekWire 确认了 6 万这个数字。

6 万人占多少？微软年报显示，截至今年 6 月 30 日，全职员工 22.3 万人。6 万除以 22.3 万约等于 27%，和流传的“约 27%”对得上。不过 22.3 万是 7 月裁员之前的数字，按现在的人数算，比例会再高一点（这是我按公开数字推算的）。

【谁能拿到】

要同时满足三个条件。所在国家是美国、加拿大、英国或印度；所在团队参加了这个计划，内部信说参不参加要看各业务的优先级、对客户的承诺和人手需求；职级在微软内部 70 级及以下。

70 级包括总经理和部分挂“副总裁”头衔的人，但不包括“企业副总裁”（CVP，微软更高一级的高管）。所以“副总裁及以下都能拿”的说法不够准确，准确说法是部分副总裁也在范围内。

不看年龄，不看工龄，也不看绩效。

哪些团队在名单上，微软没有公开。The Verge 引述知情人士说，Copilot、CoreAI、Windows 与设备、Xbox、财务和人力资源团队的员工都能申请；Cloud + AI、Microsoft AI 等部门部分参加；销售、市场、安全、量子计算等部门不参加。

【能拿到什么】

补偿和标准遣散费相当：按工龄和职级给一笔工资，股票继续按原计划到账，保留一段时间的医疗保险，再加职业转型服务。符合条件的员工会收到邮件，12 月第一周前做决定。据 Business Insider 看到的备忘录，接受的人在年底离开。

【这算裁员吗】

走不走由员工自己选，所以不算裁员。但微软也说，这个计划不能替代裁员，之后还裁不裁，要看业务情况。微软发言人表示，这不代表公司需要更少的人；据 https://t.co/g7e8n9jyIR 转述，即使员工接受了邀约，公司仍可能设法留住顶尖人才。

微软没有预测会有多少人接受，只说比例会比春季那次低得多。今年春天，微软第一次推出自愿退休计划，只面向美国、年龄加工龄达到门槛的员工，约 8750 人符合条件，约 30% 接受了，微软为此计入 9 亿美元费用。那次还多给了延长的医疗保险，这次没有。

【为什么是现在】

Bloomberg 把这次邀约称为微软最新一轮降本措施。微软正在 AI 数据中心上大量投钱，同时持续压缩人员开支：今年 7 月裁了 4800 人，其中 Xbox 约 3200 人；9 月又裁了几百人；2025 年全年裁员超过 1.5 万人。

Amy Coleman 在内部信里说，这个计划让参加的部门“多了一种方式，让团队人员适应不断变化的需求”。微软周三发布季度财报，可能会披露这次计划的预计成本。

来源：
微软官方博客，Amy Coleman 内部信《Introducing a Voluntary Exit Offer》（2026-10-26）
Bloomberg：https://t.co/69jDC8V75O

text:
你被封的 Claude 账号里，可能贡献了 Anthropic 的 7% 营收，

发现一个非常魔幻的事情，我们被封过的号，被 Anthropic 写进了他们的招股说明书的营收里，拿去给华尔街看。。

这话我没瞎编。Anthropic 在招股书里自己写的，他们即将冲刺人类历史上最大 IPO。

一、Anthropic 自己承认了什么

S-1 的 MD&A 部分有一段，我翻成人话：我们的收入里，过去有、以后也还会有一部分钱，来自那些后来被我们认定违反 usage policy 或 commercial terms 的客户。我们认为这在行业里很常见。

然后是这句关键的：根据我们的检测和审查流程，我们估计，截至 2026 年 9 月 30 日的前九个月，这类客户贡献的收入约占总收入的 5% 到 7%。

5% 到 7%，意味着一百块钱里，有五到七块，来自后来被它自己判定违规的人。

后面它还补了一句：这个估计需要判断，以后检测方法变了、又翻出以前没发现的违规用量，这个数还可能变。

翻译一下：7% 可能还算保守的。

二、钱先收，号后封

最有画面的是这句原文：
Because detection, investigation, and enforcement take time, we recognize revenue from such customers when the related services are provided, before restricting or terminating their access.

意思是：发现、调查、执法，都要时间。服务一交付，收入就确认了。限制或终止访问，排在后面。

周一，你充了值，开跑。token 哗哗地流，账单一笔一笔记上去。
周三，Anthropic 的财务系统里，这笔钱已经安安稳稳躺成了「已确认收入」
同一时间，风控那边，你的号还在调查队列里排队。前面还有几千个。
两周后，你邮箱里弹出一封信：Your account has been suspended.
你打开后台一看，钱是花完了的。服务是用过了的。收入是早就记好了的。
一切都很合规。除了你号没了

三、7% 到底是多少钱

先上铁板数。
S-1 合并利润表：2026 年上半年（截至 6 月 30 日），Revenue $16,286 million，也就是 162.86 亿美元。

接下来的数字，请把「粗算」两个字刻在脑门上。

S-1 的摘要表没有披露前九个月的营收合计。媒体公开口径：2026 年 Q3 营收约 168 亿美元

粗算：162.86 亿 + 约 168 亿 ≈ 前九个月约 330 亿美元量级

粗算：330 亿 × 5%–7% ≈ 16 亿～23 亿美元

再强调一遍：16 亿到 23 亿，是我用官方上半年数字加媒体 Q3 口径估出来的量级。官方只给了 5%–7% 这个比例，没给这个美元数。

但量级摆在那。十几二十亿美元。那是一群「后来被封的人」一起交的学费。

你那个号，在里面占了一个小小的像素。

四、8 月、9 月：阵亡潮

如果你是今年 8 月、9 月被封的，恭喜，你赶上了大部队。

S-1 原文写得很直白：公司加强了检测和执法力度，in particular in August and September 2026，尤其是 8 月和 9 月。

那两个月，大概就是风控队列突然提速。排了很久的号，一批一批被叫号，一批一批下线。

很多人在群里问「我啥也没干怎么也封了」，时间线基本对得上。

Anthropic 也说了后果：它预期违规客户的收入占比，未来会下降。

然后补了一句很诚实的话：这对营收和营收增长会造成多大拖累、什么时候拖累，不确定。

翻译成人话：号封多了，钱也会少。少多少，它自己也没底。

一家公司在招股书里，把「我们正在亲手砍掉一部分收入」写进去，还附上一句「影响多大不好说」。这段我读了两遍，挺有意思的。

五、我的看法

封号不退款这事，Anthropic 有它的规则，可以说刷新了人类商业规则下限。

这个结构真的很黑色幽默：你被封的那一刻，在你那边是「出事了」。但在它的账本上，你早就是「已完成交付」了。

你以为你被踢出了游戏。其实你的那份，已经算进了上市前的成绩单里。

参考链接：https://t.co/rj4AAgNseo
